description:
FILED s484 (Fable review of s484a, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING: identical on main 8c8fa4c0 and on the s484a tree 186134ce (the #1628 fix touches wrong-KIND referents, not undef ones).

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl, `use strict`):
    my $u; my $x = $$u[0]; print defined $u ? ref($u) : "undef";   # perl: ARRAY   PCL: undef
    my $w; my $y = $$w{k}; print ref($w);                          # perl: HASH    PCL: ""
    my $v; $$v[0] = 1;     print ref($v);                          # perl: ARRAY   PCL: ARRAY  (the WRITE side is right)

perl vivifies the CONTAINER of an element access even on the READ path (rv2av/rv2hv under an aelem/helem carry the vivify flag); only a WHOLE-aggregate rvalue cast (`@$u`) leaves undef alone -- and under strict that one dies, which is #1543's shape (its die half is out of scope: strict refs is not modelled).  #1241 (s473b) made the read path vivify every INTERMEDIATE container of a chain (`$h{a}{b}` creates $h{a}); this is the same rule at the ROOT when the root is a plain scalar VARIABLE rather than an element -- `$$u[0]` is `${$u}[0]`, and $u is the container of the subscript.

Discriminate first: does the `p-viv-container` marker path (#1241) simply not fire when the container operand is a bare variable, or does the emitter take a different arm for `$$u[0]` vs `$u->[0]` (probe both spellings, and `${$u}[0]`, and the hash twins)?  Then ONE fix at the shared chain walker, never a per-spelling arm.

BAR: the probe lines above + `$u->[0]` / `$u->{k}` read spellings + a nested `$$u[0][1]` + the whole-aggregate `@$u` which must STAY undef (#1543's value half) vs perl; guard rows beside the #1241 rows (grep Pl/t for "p-viv-container" / autoviv); corpus-diff (an emitter change) + the full sweep + `tools/ir-conform --jobs 2` (the B6 autoviv cases).  SIZE: S-M.
subject: rvalue element access through an UNDEF plain scalar does not vivify it: `my $u; my $x = $$u[0]; ref $u` is ARRAY in perl, undef in PCL (the root-scalar residue of #1241)
